options: A logically isolated, customer-defined slice of private address space inside one AWS Region
A physical data center AWS dedicates to a single customer
A global address space shared automatically across all AWS customers
A billing construct with no effect on networking
questions.explain: A VPC is AWS's name for the isolated virtual network idea — the same concept the Azure course covered as a VNet.

questions.q: What size range must a VPC's primary CIDR block fall within?
options: There is no size limit at all
questions.explain: AWS requires a VPC's primary CIDR block to be sized somewhere between /16 (about 65,000 addresses) and /28 (16 addresses).

questions.q: What happens to a subnet's Availability Zone once the subnet is created?
options: It's fixed — a subnet is pinned to exactly one AZ for its entire life and never spans AZs
AWS automatically spreads the subnet's addresses across every AZ in the Region
The AZ can be changed later with a single CLI flag
Subnets don't have an Availability Zone at all
questions.explain: A subnet is created inside exactly one Availability Zone; a design that needs resilience across AZs requires multiple matching subnets.

questions.q: How many IP addresses does AWS reserve in every subnet, regardless of its size?
questions.explain: AWS reserves the network address, the VPC router, two addresses for DNS/future use, and the broadcast address — 5 total — in every subnet.

questions.q: Why can't two subnets in the same VPC have overlapping CIDR ranges?
options: AWS rejects the create-subnet call if the range overlaps a sibling subnet's range
Overlapping ranges are allowed and routed automatically by priority
Only the first subnet created in a VPC is checked for overlap
Overlap is only a problem across different VPCs, never within one
questions.explain: Each subnet's CIDR range must fit inside the VPC's block and must not overlap any sibling subnet, or AWS refuses the request.
